values.metric: PCE price index excluding food and energy

revisions: BEA updated April and May estimates using revised BLS CES data and revised government social benefits data.

analysis.headline: US real PCE rose 0.4% in June while the PCE price index fell 0.1% month-on-month; nominal income growth slowed to 0.2%.
changes: Nominal PCE grew 0.3%, down from 0.9% in May, while real PCE held at 0.4%.
Headline PCE prices fell 0.1% month-on-month after a 0.5% May increase; core PCE prices rose 0.1% after 0.3%.
BEA revised April and May estimates.
analysis.behavioral_readout: The combination is more consistent with real spending holding up despite slower nominal income growth because the monthly PCE price index fell; it does not establish a durable consumption acceleration from one month.
implications: Inference: June reduced short-run price pressure in this measure while real consumption remained positive.
alternative_explanations: Monthly price movements and revised source data can reverse in subsequent releases.
The aggregate cannot identify which household income groups changed spending.
verification_needed: BEA July personal income and outlays release on 26 August 2026.
Subsequent revisions to April-June personal income and outlays.
caveats: PCE price and CPI are distinct measures.
April and May were revised in this release.

official_citations.label: BEA personal income and outlays, June 2026
